title: What are the best online 3D model generators, and which ones can create models from text or images?
author: its_not_me143
selftext:
A need to make a couple of prototype assets without having to install heavy software or

learning a whole 3D workflow first, is what prompted me to start playing with 3D model

generators online. Initially, I was concerned with whether a tool could produce something in

a short amount of time, but quickly realized that how the thing was put in affects the thing

out.

Text prompts are helpful when I just have a general idea and wish to try out various shapes

and styles. While the relationships between the images can still be ambiguous with only one

image, reference images offer additional visual guidance. If you are looking for a more

detailed asset, it is perhaps more suitable to start off with multiple views.

I was researching such a browser-based workflow and stumbled upon Tripo AI. It offers

text-to-3D, single-image-to-3D and multi-view generation, all in an online workspace, so I

can experiment with various input methods without having to switch the platform. The

models created can also be exported in common formats for additional editing or printing.

Nevertheless, before using any model generated I would check the geometry, proportions,

topology, textures and scale.

Do you find that it is easier for you to get consistent results from text prompts or reference

images, when using online 3D generators regularly?
